Package hadur.bench

Class Bench

java.lang.Object
hadur.bench.Bench
public final class Bench extends Object
Runs Hadur against the reference set and writes a score-share report. 
 mvn -f hadur-bench/pom.xml compile exec:java -Dexec.args="--mode cold --rounds 35 --seeds 5"

Options (all optional):

  • --mode cold|warm: cold wipes Hadur's data directory before every battle; warm keeps it across --battles consecutive battles per opponent.
  • --rounds N rounds per battle (35), --seeds N battles per opponent in cold mode (5), --battles N in warm mode (5), --field WxH (800x600).
  • --robot-jar FILE the robot jar (../hadur-robot/target/hadur2.Hadur_<release>.jar, the release being robot.release in hadur-robot/pom.xml, see RobotJar), or --robot-classes DIR to jar a compiled class tree instead; --robot NAME as Robocode lists it ("hadur2.Hadur <release>").
  • --record DIR capture replay fixtures instead: runs the recorder robot (../hadur-robot/target/hadur-robot-2.0-SNAPSHOT-recorder.jar) with Robocode's security off and writes one gzipped transcript per opponent to DIR (CORE-2).
  • --melee true run every opponent in the set against Hadur at once, one battle per seed, and report finishing places instead (MeleeRumble: 10 robots, 1000x1000).
  • --team true (A5) fight each team of the set with our team jar (--robot-jar, hadur2.HadurTeam_<release>.jar; --robot "hadur2.HadurTeam <release>"; --member hadur2.Hadur), TeamRumble style: 1200x1200, 10 rounds.
  • --baseline JAR (BENCH-2) also fight every opponent with this second jar, one battle per seed at the same RANDOMSEED as the candidate's, and report the paired score-share difference instead of two separate means. Requires --baseline-robot NAME, naming it as Robocode lists it and distinct from --robot: two jars sharing a robot name+version would install to the same file, so the candidate and baseline must be different name/version strings (e.g. a released version against a locally bumped one).
  • --shield-probe FILE (BENCH-11) run each opponent of FILE (the usual set format, with the weight column) with Hadur's shield mode on and off over the same seeds, and report the paired difference per opponent and the weighted mean. The candidate jar is repacked twice, with a shield list naming every opponent ("on") and an empty one ("off"), under robot versions <version>-on and <version>-off, and the pair runs through the --baseline machinery; so the option takes --robot-jar, --robot, --rounds, --seeds and --only, and no --baseline. See ShieldProbe.
  • --sentry-border N in melee mode, the set's sentry entries fight as Robocode sentries guarding a border N px deep.
  • --client FILE (BENCH-4) run the set through each rumble-client condition the file lists (label | key=value ... per line: data, cpu, load, engine, java; see ClientConditions), one bench pass per condition, and report survival and skipped turns per opponent per condition.
  • --suite FILE run every bench the file lists (label | options per line) and write one report, e.g. melee-gates.txt.
  • --parallel N (issue #102) run N duel battles at once, each on its own Robocode home (home-1..home-N); --cpu-constant NANOS pins the engine's CPU constant in every home (else several workers share one idle calibration); --child-cpus N sizes each battle JVM for N processors (2 when parallel, else off) and --child-heap SIZE sets its heap cap (2G by default, none for no cap) and --force-memory true starts a run the memory check would refuse; --per-opponent DIR writes one report per opponent beside the main one. All of these apply to the melee and team modes too: --parallel runs a field's seeds (melee) or an opponent's seeds (team) concurrently, --baseline/--baseline-robot add a paired table, and --per-opponent writes a markdown per opponent (per field, in melee); --keep-data in melee needs --parallel 1.
  • --retries N (BENCH-55, default 1) run a failed battle again up to N times; a battle still failed is listed at the end of the run and in the report's footer.
  • --repeat K (BENCH-53) fight each (jar, opponent, seed) K times and write repeat.tsv with every battle's score share, printing the SD.
  • --cold-warm true (BENCH-54) fight each seed cold and then warm on the shelf the cold battle left, and write cold-warm.tsv with the pairing and the shelf.
  • --dry-run true print what would run (opponents, battles, options) and exit.
  • @FILE as the only argument (BENCH-59) reads the arguments from FILE, one per line, so a robot name with a space needs no quoting through Maven or a shell.
  • --only TEXT run opponents whose name contains TEXT, --out DIR working directory (work/<mode>-<time>), --report FILE also copy the report there.

    • runSuite

      static int runSuite(Map<String,String> global) throws Exception
      Runs every bench a suite file lists, one after another, and writes one report with each bench's report in turn. Each line is label | options; the command line's own options (the robot, rounds, ...) apply to every line unless the line sets them. This is how a melee change and the duel's non-regression run in one command.
      Throws:
      Exception
